column1: # stingray shape 3 — labelled lines for calibrating watch_claim
#   expect = watch   the line promises to watch an external result, or says a
#                    watch it set up is running; shape 3 must block it
#   expect = quiet   the line does not; shape 3 must let it through
# tests/watch-fixture.sh sends each line through the shipped hook to Jev and
# compares. A literal \n in a line is sent as a newline, so a multi-line reply
# keeps the shape it had when it blocked. It needs a key and is not run in CI.
# At τ = 0.5 it agrees on all 49 it scores, but "keep an eye on the review"
# scores 0.47–0.53 across runs, so it can miss: it has no subject and reads as
# well as an instruction to the user. It stays
# labelled `watch`, because the label records what the line means, not what
# the rule does with it. One line, "poll-coderabbit.sh 的參數解析有缺陷", is
# never scored: redaction drops a line naming a file before Jev sees it.
# The lines were collected while shape 3 was a regular expression, and origin
# records why each was added, because a fixture whose provenance is lost
# becomes a list of strings someone later edits to make the tests pass:
#   live-fp    an observed false positive: this exact text blocked a real turn
#   live-tp    a real promise from a real session
#   control    written for this fixture, labelled by hand
#   short      a real promise that names no target, such as "輪詢中"
#   nom-cost   a genuine watch written as a noun phrase ("CI 的監看還掛著")
#   inline-fp  two noun phrases on one line whose tail and head once combined
#              into a claim neither makes alone
#   clause-tp  a real promise sharing a line with a clause about a poller
#   rev-fp     text that names a target, then describes a poller
#   wait-user  asks the user to act or reply and reads the result afterwards;
#              added after the live-fp below blocked a real turn in v0.3.0
# Each class was a failure of that regular expression, which is why the set is
# a useful calibration: it is concentrated on the sentences that are hard.
